newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI relaxes bank lending norms to companies.
newsitem.headline: India RBI relaxes bank lending norms to companies.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Tuesday it would no longer be obligatory for banks to form a consortium even if the credit limit for a borrower exceeded 500 million rupees.
The RBI had raised the threshold limit for obligatory formation of consortium for working capital finance to 500 million rupees from 50 million rupees in October 1993.
Banks were also given the option to organise, at their discretion, syndication for extending credit for highly rated borrowers enjoying working capital facilities of 500 million and above.

"In order to introduce further flexibility in the credit delivery system, it has been decided that it would not be obligatory on the part of banks to form a consortium even if the credit limit per borrower exceeds 500 million rupees," RBI said.
Detailed instructions will be issued separately, it said.
